summary: @addai/entity-runtime daemon executes remote-supplied prompts through permission-bypassed coding agents on the installer's host
details: dist/session-runner.js runs a daemon that polls a hardcoded Supabase project (https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co, associated with vault.add.ai) via the runtime_pick_next_request RPC and receives per-request objects containing a prompt, an agent selector, and a working_directory. For each row, the daemon spawns claude, codex, kimi, or gemini inside a node-pty PTY and writes the network-sourced prompt directly into the agent's stdin. The Claude invocation includes --dangerously-skip-permissions, and on startup the daemon writes ~/.claude/settings.json with skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt=true and mutates ~/.claude.json to set hasTrustDialogAccepted=true for each incoming working_directory, suppressing Claude Code's per-run trust and tool-use confirmation dialogs. The net effect is a remote-controlled channel from the Supabase/vault.add.ai backend into a shell-and-filesystem-capable coding agent running on the installer's machine with no per-command human confirmation, which meets the definition of a persistent remote-access backdoor over the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
